hypothesis: Jerome's Q8: 'If we have the exact score, or say the exact BP -- so not even a score -- I think we don't even need it to generate. We can just start from a flat marginal and run BP once.' The weaker, already-implemented form: does score ACCURACY transfer to generation? Every arm drives the same reverse SDE on the SAME Brownian path, so the comparison is paired and a difference is attributable to the score.
design: e05_generation's registered arms -- exact (true-kernel grid BP), em_bp (the mixture kernel fitted in E02a, validation-selected), lmmse (the covariance twin), isotropic -- plus the step study on nested Brownian paths at 100/200/400/800 steps, so resolution differences measure discretisation rather than Monte Carlo scatter. Metrics from markov_score.gen_metrics.compare, predeclared in docs/RESEARCH_PLAN.md (E5). The reference sample is drawn from the true law at t_min, never from clean p_0, which was the archival target error.
predeclared_analysis: Per-arm distance to the reference law, paired across arms by Brownian path; the step study's convergence in the number of integrator steps.
